key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination, but thermal aging causes faster degradation with losses extending into the perovskite absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive measurements can help engineers distinguish interface and bulk degradation when evaluating perovskite passivation strategies.
method: Measure photoluminescence under multiple excitation wavelengths.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced fullerene-induced interfacial losses after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging, with simulations supporting interface-versus-bulk interpretations.
watch_item: Depth attribution is model-supported rather than direct imaging, and the abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
